meta.title: Course Knowledge Graph
meta.description: Concept map for CS3103 mid-term quiz prep (Lec 1–5): interrupts, processes/threads, scheduling, synchronization. Not a lecture folder tree.

nodes.label: OS roles (allocator + control)
nodes.detail: OS sits between apps and hardware; allocates CPU/memory/devices; controls execution for safety.

nodes.label: Interrupts / timer / DMA
nodes.detail: HW/SW interrupts drive the OS; timer enables preemption; DMA moves blocks with one interrupt per block.

nodes.label: User vs kernel mode
nodes.detail: Mode bit; privileged instructions only in kernel; illegal use traps to OS.

nodes.label: System calls / API
nodes.detail: Controlled door into kernel; apps usually call APIs (printf→write). Mode switch ≠ process context switch.

nodes.label: Mode switch vs context switch
nodes.detail: Mode switch: same process, change privilege. Context switch: save/load PCB (or thread regs), change who owns CPU.

nodes.label: Process + PCB + states
nodes.detail: Program in execution; PCB holds CPU state, memory, files. States: new/ready/running/waiting/terminated.

nodes.label: fork / IPC / RPC
nodes.detail: fork returns 0 in child, child PID in parent. IPC: shared memory vs message passing; RPC = remote call via messages + stubs.

nodes.label: Threads + Pthreads
nodes.detail: Lightweight unit sharing address space; create/join; cancellation async vs deferred.

nodes.label: Concurrency vs parallelism
nodes.detail: Concurrency = interleaved progress (even 1 core); parallelism = simultaneous on multiple cores.

nodes.label: Context switch mechanics
nodes.detail: Save regs to per-task stack; switch SP; restore; fake initial stack frame for new task. Overhead, no useful work.

nodes.label: Scheduler vs dispatcher
nodes.detail: Short-term scheduler picks next ready task; dispatcher does context switch + user mode + jump. Dispatch latency = overhead.

nodes.label: Scheduling criteria
nodes.detail: Maximize utilization/throughput; minimize turnaround/waiting/response. Goals conflict.

nodes.label: FCFS / SJF / SRTF
nodes.detail: FCFS convoy effect; SJF optimal avg wait (needs burst estimate via exp. averaging); SRTF = preemptive SJF.

nodes.label: Priority / RR / MLFQ
nodes.detail: Priority + aging vs starvation; RR quantum tradeoff; multilevel feedback moves tasks between queues.

nodes.label: SMP / affinity / CFS
nodes.detail: Symmetric multiprocessor scheduling; load balancing vs processor affinity; Linux CFS uses vruntime + nice.

nodes.label: Race + critical section
nodes.detail: Shared data + non-atomic RMW → races. CS needs mutual exclusion, progress, bounded waiting.

nodes.label: Peterson / TestAndSet / Swap
nodes.detail: Software ME for 2 processes; hardware atomic ops enable spinlocks.

nodes.label: Semaphore (P/V)
nodes.detail: wait/signal; binary=mutex; counting=resources. Busy-wait vs block/wakeup queues.

nodes.label: Bounded buffer
nodes.detail: empty=N, full=0, mutex=1. wait resource before mutex or deadlock. signal order mainly efficiency.

nodes.label: Readers–Writers / Dining
nodes.detail: Many readers or one writer; dining chopsticks can deadlock if all take left first.

nodes.label: Monitor + condition vars
nodes.detail: Language-enforced ME; wait/signal on conditions (bank counter analogy).

nodes.label: Deadlock (intro)
nodes.detail: Circular wait for locks/semaphores; four conditions; elaboration next chapter.

nodes.label: Mid-term quiz (15%)
nodes.detail: Catalogue: CA 40% = assignments 17% + case study 8% + mid-term quiz 15%; final 60%. Exact date on Canvas.
